question: Does parameter induction generalize to multi-parameter mechanisms with multiple distinct varying fields (path, body, headers) and distinct slot naming, when training observations come from synthetic but structurally realistic multi-field mechanisms?
hypothesis: When multiple observations of the same intent share identical preconditions and postconditions but vary across multiple fields (path segments, body values, header values), parameter induction correctly: (1) identifies each independently varying field as a distinct parameter slot, (2) assigns distinct slot names per varying field location, (3) produces an action template where each slot can be independently substituted, and (4) resolves to EXECUTABLE with correct bound_action for unseen parameter combinations that were never jointly observed in training.
falsifier: Parameter induction fails to produce distinct slots for distinct varying fields (collapses multiple fields into one slot or misses a varying field entirely), OR bound_action substitutes the wrong value into the wrong slot, OR resolution fails for any unseen parameter combination, OR positive control fails (seen identifier resolution), OR null control fails (mismatched preconditions resolve instead of abstaining).
baselines: B1_cold: Cold exploration — no memory, simulated full-task cost (estimated 5 operations: authenticate, navigate, fill body, set headers, submit).
B2_literal: Literal mechanism replay — mechanism with no parameter slots, cannot bind new identifiers; expected to fail on all unseen combinations.

B3_single_slot: Single-slot mechanism — mechanism induced by collapsing all varying fields into one param_name='id' slot (current kernel limitation); expected to fail when multiple independent parameters are needed.
positive_control: Resolution with all seen training identifiers (resource=A, title='Alpha', token='tok-A') returns EXECUTABLE with correct bound_action matching the original observation.
null_control: Resolution with mismatched preconditions (authenticated=False when mechanism requires authenticated=True) returns UNKNOWN (abstains).
measurement_validity: All observations are synthetic and deterministic; no model calls or browser interactions.
Training set contains 3 observations with distinct resource/title/token combinations.
Test set contains 10 unseen combinations never jointly observed in training.
Parameter induction is performed before resolution testing; no outcome data influences induction design.
Resolution uses the same kernel.resolve() interface as the previous experiment.
Confidence threshold (0.8) and min_confidence logic are unchanged from previous experiment.
decision_rule: SURVIVES if ALL of: (1) parameter induction identifies >= 3 distinct parameter slots (one per varying field: resource, title, token), (2) unseen_resolution_rate >= 90% (9/10 unseen combinations resolve to EXECUTABLE), (3) binding_accuracy = 100% (all resolved bound_actions have correct substitutions in correct slots), (4) single_slot_baseline fails on all unseen combinations (literal_fail_rate = 100%), (5) positive_control passes (seen combination resolves to EXECUTABLE), (6) null_control passes (mismatched preconditions resolve to UNKNOWN). Otherwise FALSIFIED.
product_consequence_positive: Multi-parameter induction is viable at the kernel level. The mechanism generalizes beyond single-field parameterization. This strengthens C-PARAM-INHERIT toward multi-field mechanisms and justifies proceeding to noisy/real-browser observation testing. Product architecture can support mechanisms with multiple independent parameter slots.
product_consequence_negative: If multi-parameter induction fails (collapses slots or misassigns names), C-PARAM-INHERIT remains limited to single-field mechanisms. Product cannot support complex mechanisms like POST endpoints with body + path parameters. Kernel design must be reconsidered before further product investment in parameterized inheritance.
estimated_cost: Very low: pure synthetic data, offline computation, no browser/network/model calls. 3 training observations, 10 test combinations, 3 baselines, 2 controls.
expected_information_gain: High: directly tests the handoff-identified next step for C-PARAM-INHERIT. A positive result extends the claim ceiling from single-parameter to multi-parameter. A negative result identifies a concrete kernel limitation. The experiment is minimal (same synthetic framework, extended observations) and has clear discriminating power.
